newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea bond yields end lower on eased liquidity.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea bond yields end lower on eased liquidity.

text.p: Benchmark bond yields closed sharply lower on Thursday in active trade on the back of improving short-term cash liquidity, dealers said.
They said traders actively bought bonds as liquidity continued to improve despite earlier expectations of shortages ahead of the Korean Thanksgiving holidays.
* 3-yr corporates close at 12.07 pct vs Wednesday's 12.18
* 3-mth CDs end at 14.00 pct vs Wednesday's 14.65
* Overnight call average unchanged at 13.50 pct
Yields on three-month CDs closed sharply lower because commercial banks, flush with short-term cash, reduced new issues, dealers said.
Cash demand usually picks up ahead of the Chusok holidays but this year liquidity showed no signs of tightening up, they said.
"This year the government is taking relatively flexible monetary policies to keep interest rates low, and this boosts bond buying," another dealer said.
